 Job Description 
 
 As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

 Excellent Benefits Package 
 Review our company’s Total Rewards

 Paid Time Off & Holidays

 Tuition Reimbursement – eligible after 90 days!
 Employee Referral Bonus
 Employee Discount Program
 Recognition Program

 Career Advancement Opportunities

 Role Summary 
 The AVI Software, Vision & Automation Systems Engineer configures, integrates, tests, and supports automated visual inspection (AVI) and industrial automation systems across their lifecycle. The role improves system performance, resolves technical issues, and supports deployments in manufacturing, laboratory, integration, and customer-site environments. 

 Key Responsibilities 
 •  Configure, implement, test, troubleshoot, and optimize AVI software, machine-vision applications, PLC controls, automation sequences, and system interfaces. 
 •  Translate customer, inspection, and manufacturing requirements into system configurations, recipes, control logic, and technical specifications. 
 •  Analyze inspection results, image data, and equipment behavior to improve accuracy, reliability, and operational performance; lead or support root-cause analysis and corrective actions. 
 •  Support system integration, installation, commissioning, qualification, validation, upgrades, and deployment, including change testing and verification. 
 •  Provide technical support and escalation for customer, field-service, and internal engineering issues; collaborate across software, automation, electrical, mechanical, Quality, and Operations teams. 
 •  Create and maintain clear technical specifications, configuration records, procedures, test documentation, and troubleshooting guides. 
 •  Apply engineering and field feedback while following applicable quality, regulatory, cybersecurity, and change-control requirements. 

 Education & Experience 
 •  Advanced degree plus 3 years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree plus 5 years of relevant experience, in engineering, automation, software, machine vision, or a related technical field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered. 
 •  Relevant experience with PLCs, industrial automation, machine vision, automated inspection, software-controlled equipment, manufacturing systems, or technical support. 
 •  Experience in regulated manufacturing, such as pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or life sciences, and with installation, commissioning, qualification, or validation is preferred. 

 Knowledge & Skills 
 •  Strong systems thinking, analytical troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis skills across software, vision hardware, PLCs, equipment, networks, and manufacturing processes. 
 •  Working knowledge of PLC programming, control logic, sequencing, interlocks, alarms, I/O, and industrial communication protocols; machine vision and image processing experience is highly desirable. 
 •  Understanding of system testing, configuration management, requirements, and change control; familiarity with cGMP, validation, data integrity, and quality systems is preferred. 
 •  Clear technical writing, communication, organization, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work independently and across multidisciplinary teams. 
 •  Proficiency in English; additional languages are a plus. Ability to travel up to 50%, including to customer and Thermo Fisher Scientific locations, as required.
